hook: Human cells exposed to low hydrogen sulfide store carbon in lipid droplets to offset redox stress.
summary: Chronic exposure to 4 to 20 micromolar H2S shifted NAD and coenzyme Q pools toward the reduced state and drove triglyceride buildup in lipid droplets across several human cell lines. Blocking fatty acid synthesis during exposure impaired recovery of respiration. This was seen in cultured cells, so the link to gut sulfide and metabolic health remains a hypothesis.
title: Lipid droplets buffer hydrogen sulfide-induced redox imbalance.
venue: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
